bibl.title: The Ethics of AI Ethics: An Evaluation of Guidelines

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: 22 AI ethics guidelines - which issues each one covers, which it omits, and whether any of it changes what practitioners do
span.quote: Designed as a semi-systematic evaluation, this paper analyzes and compares 22 guidelines, highlighting overlaps but also omissions. As a result, I give a detailed overview of the field of AI ethics. Finally, I also examine to what extent the respective ethical principles and values are implemented in the practice of research, development and application of AI systems—and how the effectiveness in the demands of AI ethics can be improved.

span.label: whether ethical guidelines have an actual impact on human decision-making in AI and machine learning
span.quote: However, the critical question arises: Do those ethical guidelines have an actual impact on human decision-making in the field of AI and machine learning? The short answer is: No, most often not.

span.label: a comparison of 22 guidelines that tallies coverage AND absence, sorts the absences into justified and unjustified, and states that the selection method decided the list
span.quote: Second, not all omissions can be treated equally. There are omissions which are missing or severely underrepresented without any good reason—for instance the aspect of political abuse or “hidden” social and ecological costs of AI systems—, and omissions that can be justified

span.label: critique
span.quote: However, the critical question arises: Do those ethical guidelines have an actual impact on human decision-making in the field of AI and machine learning? The short answer is: No, most often not.

span.label: a normative vocabulary assembled by many bodies at once, whose commonest terms turn out to be the ones with engineering solutions
span.quote: Especially the aspects of accountability, privacy or fairness appear altogether in about 80% of all guidelines and seem to provide the minimal requirements for building and using an “ethically sound” AI system. What is striking here is the fact that the most frequently mentioned aspects are those for which technical fixes can be or have already been developed.

span.label: a semi-systematic evaluation - 22 guidelines selected by literature analysis against stated inclusion rules, coded issue by issue with a declared marking criterion, and an explicit account of what the selection excluded
span.term: a semi-systematic evaluation - 22 guidelines selected by literature analysis against stated inclusion rules, coded issue by issue with a declared marking criterion, and an explicit account of what the selection excluded
span.quote: Designed as a semi-systematic evaluation, this paper analyzes and compares 22 guidelines, highlighting overlaps but also omissions. As a result, I give a detailed overview of the field of AI ethics. Finally, I also examine to what extent the respective ethical principles and values are implemented in the practice of research, development and application of AI systems—and how the effectiveness in the demands of AI ethics can be improved.

span.label: accountability, privacy and fairness appear in about 80% of the guidelines, and the author's observation is that these are exactly the aspects for which technical fixes exist or are being built. A NORMATIVE VOCABULARY SELECTED BY TRACTABILITY: what can be engineered gets written down, and what cannot - political abuse, ecological cost, democratic erosion - does not
span.term: the vocabulary is shaped by what is solvable
span.quote: Especially the aspects of accountability, privacy or fairness appear altogether in about 80% of all guidelines and seem to provide the minimal requirements for building and using an “ethically sound” AI system. What is striking here is the fact that the most frequently mentioned aspects are those for which technical fixes can be or have already been developed.

span.label: excluding robot ethics guidelines means the list of issues lacks robotics issues. The author states this BEFORE reporting the omissions, so every absence in the paper is already qualified by the selection that produced it - which is the discipline a negative finding needs and almost never gets
span.term: the sample decides the absence list
span.quote: First, the sampling method used to select the AI ethics guidelines has an effect on the list of issues and omissions. When deliberately excluding for instance robot ethics guidelines, this has the effect that the list of entries lacks issues that are connected with robotics.

span.label: an issue can be missing without any good reason - political abuse, hidden social and ecological costs - or missing for a reason that can be stated. The author refuses to count them together, which turns a list of gaps into two different claims
span.quote: Second, not all omissions can be treated equally. There are omissions which are missing or severely underrepresented without any good reason—for instance the aspect of political abuse or “hidden” social and ecological costs of AI systems—, and omissions that can be justified

span.label: a marker goes in only where an issue is explicitly discussed in one or more paragraphs - unless the guideline is so short that it is nothing but brief mentions, in which case brief mentions count. THE EXCEPTION IS WHERE THE MEASUREMENT WOULD OTHERWISE PENALISE BREVITY RATHER THAN SILENCE
span.term: a coding rule with its exception printed
span.quote: In Table 1, I only inserted green markers if the corresponding issues were explicitly discussed in one or more paragraphs. Isolated mentions without further explanations were not considered, unless the analyzed guideline is so short that it consists entirely of brief mentions altogether.

span.label: industry guidelines suggest to legislators that self-governance suffices and no specific laws are needed. So the existence of an ethical vocabulary is itself an argument against a binding one - the guidelines are not only a record of values, they are an intervention in whether values become rules
span.term: ethics as a substitute for law
span.quote: Ethics guidelines of the AI industry serve to suggest to legislators that internal self-governance in science and industry is sufficient, and that no specific laws are necessary to mitigate possible technological risks and to eliminate scenarios of abuse (Calo 2017).

span.label: the sampling method has an effect on the list of issues and omissions - excluding robot ethics guidelines removes robotics issues from the result
span.quote: First, the sampling method used to select the AI ethics guidelines has an effect on the list of issues and omissions. When deliberately excluding for instance robot ethics guidelines, this has the effect that the list of entries lacks issues that are connected with robotics.

span.label: the selection is biased towards western and northern documents and excludes guidelines not written in English
span.quote: In this context, a shortcoming one has to consider is that my selection is biased towards documents which are western/northern in nature, excluding guidelines which are not written in English.

span.label: the evaluation is semi-systematic rather than a full analysis of every available soft-law or non-legal norm document
